content: Various communication channels and tools can be utilized to deliver messages, provide information, and offer counseling. These include peer providers and innovative digital approaches such as videos, social media platforms, and mobile phone applications or services. Providers of HIV Testing Services (HTS) must aim to deliver high-quality testing services. Quality assurance (QA) mechanisms should be in place to ensure that individuals receive accurate diagnoses. QA measures may include both internal and external evaluations, with support from the national reference laboratory. It is essential that all individuals who receive a positive HIV diagnosis undergo retesting to confirm their diagnosis before initiating antiretroviral therapy (ART) or engaging in HIV care. Linkage to prevention, care, and treatment services must include effective and appropriate follow-up as needed, encompassing long-term prevention and treatment support. Offering HTS in areas with no access to or poor linkage to care, including ART, provides limited benefit to individuals living with HIV. Ensuring linkage to care is the responsibility of providers and testers delivering HTS.
